title: Nonnegativity conjecture for the $q$-binomial quotient $G_{k,n}(q)$
statement:
For $k,n\in\mathbb{N}_0$, define $G_{k,n}(q)$ by

$$
F_{k,1}(q)=\sum_{n\ge 0}G_{k,n}(q)q^{n+1},\qquad G_{k,n}(q)=\frac{1}{1-q^{2n+1}}\frac{\begin{bmatrix}2k+2n-2\\2n\end{bmatrix}_{q}}{\begin{bmatrix}k+n-1\
\end{bmatrix}_{q^2}}.
$$

Here $\begin{bmatrix}a\\b\end{bmatrix}_q$ denotes the $q$-binomial coefficient, and $A(q)\succeq0$ means that all coefficients of $A(q)$ are nonnegative. **Nonnegativity conjecture for $G_{k,n}(q)$.** One has $G_{k,n}(q)\succeq0$. This is a refinement of the $m=1$ positivity conjecture and would imply it; the source presents it as an open conjecture supported by the displayed quotient and computational evidence.
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2306.09450](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.09450), [arXiv:1312.7548](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.7548).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04014

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).
source_name: Koustav Banerjee, Kathrin Bringmann and William J. Keith, “On a conjecture of Andrews and Bachraoui”, arXiv:2601.04014 (2026).
